sections.heading: USING IT
lines: Bands run left to right: HPF > Low > Mid > High > LPF.
HPF / LPF: Freq (20 Hz-20 kHz) and Slope (6, 12, 18 or 24 dB/oct).
Low / Mid / High bells: Freq, Gain (+/-18 dB) and Q (0.1-10, 1 at the centre of the dial).
Character: Drive = amount of warm saturation (level stays the same). Bias = more even harmonics.
The numbers under the dials show the current values.

sections.heading: AS A BPATCHER
lines: Inlet: mono signal in. Outlet: mono signal out.
Each control has a scripting name matching its parameter (hpf_freq, bell1_gain, drive ...).
Add a pattrstorage in the parent to store and recall settings -- see gen-eq-test.maxpat.
For stereo or multichannel use gen-eq-mc.maxpat, which has the same face.

sections.heading: HOW IT WORKS
lines: gen~ gen-eq-engine: zero-delay-feedback state-variable filters, one per band.
All four slopes run in parallel and crossfade, so switching slope never clicks.
A soft, slightly asymmetric saturation sits between stages, then a DC blocker at the output.
Every parameter is smoothed inside gen~, so dial moves do not zipper.
